hypotheses.statement: The L1-supervised pair ranking acts on the intended path: the pair gradient reaches the L1 codebook only and the L1 assignments change during training.
The L1-supervised candidate satisfies P > 0.08097285816257246, N < 0.008752316503966327 and C < 0.1511367795989751 simultaneously on one checkpoint export.
Issue #274 failed because the final-q ranking let the L2/L3 codebooks absorb the ordering, so the exported L1 prefix did not move.

The geometric closed/open pair labels are not the behavioural relation that P measures, so even a correct L1 ranking of the selected pairs may not move P (the motivation for the pre-registered same-anchor round).
The curvature screen carries information beyond the closed/open label, the direct edge, the common neighbours and the degrees.
The chain-ALL signal of #283 is a proxy for the L1 codebook coarseness (the L1 collision rate), not an independent behavioural signal.
Supervising the selected L1 codeword raises P and lowers C but cannot lower N, because the encoder that decides the L1 partition receives no pair gradient.
A same-anchor behavioural contrast (a direct neighbour against a distance-two co-item) with a margin calibrated on the L1 scale lowers N without losing P.
Routing the pair gradient through the encoder with the straight-through backward lets the L1 partition become finer, so P rises while N and C fall.
hypotheses.verdict_reason: the STE path made the encoder gradient non-zero (0.0268) and the mid-training collision fell to 0.130-0.138, but the final-epoch export is coarser: P 0.08088581, N 0.00930792, C 0.15601741 (0 of 3 thresholds)

hypotheses.statement: The saturated margin (calibrated on the final-q scale) made the L1 pair term an unhinged contraction of the codebook; re-deriving it on the L1 scale makes the ranking selective and lowers N while keeping P.
hypotheses.verdict_reason: the L1-scale margin (0.0229) made the hinge active on 47% of the pairs and pulled the codebook together instead of separating it: the final-epoch collision rose to 0.1643 and the export gives P 0.08624802 (pass), N 0.01029398 (fail), C 0.16415179 (fail) - 1 of 3 thresholds

hypotheses.statement: The measured P-N trade-off of rounds 1-4 comes from the positive pair being adjacent: a same-anchor ranking whose positive is a non-adjacent behavioural co-occurrence partner (an item that shares a neighbour with the anchor) and whose negative comes from another centre lowers N below 0.008752316503966327 while keeping P above 0.08097285816257246 and C below 0.1511367795989751.
hypotheses.verdict_reason: the non-adjacent positive moved the trade-off in the predicted direction (N 0.010144 -> 0.009581 against round 2, i.e. the anchor's L1 bucket no longer drags in a direct group, and C 0.158376 -> 0.157888) but it cost P (0.085064 -> 0.082453) and stayed on the curve: P 0.08245269 (pass), N 0.00958146 (fail), C 0.15788831 (fail) - 1 of 3 thresholds

hypotheses.statement: The P-N trade-off is not a property of the term's strength but of the negative construction: a ranking whose negative is a measured false positive (an item that already shares the anchor's L1 code and has no observed relation with it), stated on the item representation so that the separation instruction has a gradient, lowers N below 0.008752316503966327 while keeping P above 0.08097285816257246 and C below 0.1511367795989751.
hypotheses.verdict_reason: the hard-negative construction raised P the most of the whole family (0.088198, above every earlier round and both reference arms) and the measured path confirms its premise (the ranking accuracy 0.262, i.e. the mined false positives were closer than the behavioural positives; the margin satisfaction 0.0098; the pair gradient reached the encoder at lambda 3.864e-05; the mined pool fell from 267.6 to 219.7 items at epoch 500), but N rose with P (0.010533) and C stayed high (0.158864) - 1 of 3 thresholds.  Separating the mined items does not lower N because the partition re-equilibrates: the Sinkhorn balance keeps the bucket sizes, so removing one false positive moves another item into the bucket.  N is a property of the assignment structure, not of the individual pairs

pre_registration.margin_rule: |median(d_negative - d_positive)| on the frozen TIGER checkpoint's item representation over the frozen hard-negative index, computed before the run
